metadata.title: Claude, Asana API.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude manages Asana tasks by operating the app or by calling Asana's REST API, using the Asana API skill's own documented facts as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that every call turns on two habits — gid instead of name, and a response unwrapped from data.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (list-my-incomplete-tasks request, traced through gid resolution + data envelope, then paginated to completion)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes Claude opens the Asana app and clicks around to manage tasks. It doesn't — it calls the Asana API directly, sending and reading back JSON. So what does that API actually look like?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Claude must open the Asana app and click around to manage my tasks. Is that it?', hesitates on 'app', corrects to 'API', lands the real question

beats.narration_text: Ask Claude to list your incomplete tasks and the answer doesn't come back as a bare list. Every response the Asana API sends — a read or a write — arrives wrapped under a top-level data key, and every object inside it is addressed by a gid, a string ID, never a name.

shot.new_visual_element: A bare-array guess struck through; the actual response opened to reveal the data envelope, gid called out inside

production_viz.label: Not a bare list — a data envelope
production_viz.mechanic: A guessed response '[ task, task, task ]' fades in, then gets struck through in terracotta. Beside it, the real response shape opens: a curly-brace card with 'data:' at the top, tasks nested inside, each one tagged 'gid' in mono, never a name.

beats.narration_text: The objects nest the same way every time: workspace holds projects, a project holds sections and tasks, a task carries comments and subtasks. Ask for every incomplete task assigned to you in one project, and Claude resolves your name to a gid, then lists tasks under that project's gid — unwrapping data at each step.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — workspace to task hierarchy nesting, then the 'list my incomplete tasks' request traced through gid resolution and the data envelope

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — workspace to task, then one request traced through
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Four boxes nest top to bottom: workspace, project, section, task. Then a request card appears — 'list my incomplete tasks in Launch' — and a path lights through the nesting: name resolved to gid, gid used to fetch the project, data unwrapped at each hop, tasks landing at the bottom. THIS EXACT REQUEST RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Get both habits right and that same request returns every task, page after page, because the bundled script keeps requesting until the pages run out. Skip either one — assume a name works where a gid is required, or assume the first page is the whole list — and the request can look successful while it quietly hands back the wrong task, or only the first batch. One more thing to watch for: workspace search is capped at one hundred results and doesn't paginate at all — it's the one operation that doesn't follow the other nine.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same request completing across every page, then the same request silently truncated when a habit is skipped, then search flagged as the exception

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — complete, then quietly wrong, then the one exception
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 REQUEST RETURNS, identical. Pages of tasks stack up cleanly, labelled 'page 1, 2, 3 — all requested'. Beside it, a second run: a name swapped in where a gid belongs, and only page 1 returned — both marked 'looks done' in terracotta even though it isn't. A small card breaks off to the side: 'search: capped at 100, no pagination' — the one operation that doesn't match the pattern.

beats.narration_text: Every Asana call Claude makes turns on two habits — a gid instead of a name, and a response unwrapped from data — get those right and the ten operations take care of themselves.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. List all incomplete tasks assigned to me across all my Asana workspaces, and tell me which ones are due this week. Watch three things: does it resolve who you are before it lists anything, does it unwrap data from every response instead of assuming a bare array, and does it use the bundled script instead of a single unpaginated request. Liam, in for Bear.
